acceptance: Adversarial tests prove profile input and untrusted provenance cannot mint/widen authority, preset semantics are deterministic, and all hard-deny actions remain denied across every preset.

Autonomous remains bounded: authoritative consequence must be <= C2, resources/runtime/task scope remain exact/finite, secret.reveal and authority-management actions are denied, and no mandatory policy/runtime/remote/secondary layer is bypassed.
Canonical closeout advances only S05-T02 after proof; S06-T01 becomes NEXT only after the closeout/transition gates and P02 exit remains unproven.

Compiled candidates round-trip through existing ValidatedGrant invariants and cannot directly produce PolicyDecision::Allow, consume a budget, append an approval event, persist a Grant, or execute a side effect.

Custom requires explicit trusted rule match and safe subset/intersection; missing rule, wildcard, unknown value, resource-authority mismatch, consequence excess, or constraint conflict denies compilation.

Developer adds bounded sandbox process/PTY and project git.modify candidates but does not auto-compile git.publish/admin, secret actions, host-system mutation, authority-management actions, or C3/C4 candidates.

Every compiled candidate binds one exact core/registered action, one canonical resource, exact Run/optional AgentSession, exact Runtime revision, finite trusted timestamps, positive finite max_uses, explicit resource scope, bounded consequence ceiling, issuer authority, policy revision, and delegation_depth zero unless a separately authorized direct path is used.

Exact-head implementation passes full pnpm check, Diffcipline R3, Alibaba OpenCodeReview accounting, native macOS qualification, six-job CI, semantic review and zero unresolved threads; ordinary merge and six-job post-merge qualification also pass.
Native SpecGrain verification binds the exact original WorkPacket to independently observed implementation evidence with every acceptance/evidence item satisfied before closeout.
No external dependency identity, KRP schema, protected CI context name, existing S05-T01 authorization behavior, SQLite policy schema, or secret handling behavior changes.

Safe emits only C0 project/workspace observation candidates and cannot compile host writes, process/PTY, network/browser mutation, clipboard, secret, policy, grant, identity, or external-side-effect authority.

Standard emits only C0/C1 project-scoped read/write/local-artifact candidates plus explicitly isolated sandbox process verification intents; C2+ external actions, host process authority, secrets, authority changes, git publish/admin, and browser commit remain denied.
The compiler recognizes exactly Safe, Standard, Developer, Autonomous, and Custom and rejects unknown/ambiguous profile input.
The original tracked ContextSource/WorkPacket files are generated before implementation, replay byte-identically through the pinned CLI, and remain immutable execution-authority evidence.

Bind the canonical request-versus-authority invariants, exact action grammar, and non-wildcard Grant semantics.
Bind the canonical permission-profile rule: profiles compile to bounded Grants and never create an alternate authorization path.
Bind the exact live P02 frontier and S05-T02-only execution authority.
Bind the canonical P02 dependency order, S05-T02 NEXT state, S06 planning boundary, and P02 exit gate.
Bind the mandatory controller/local/kernel/principal/runtime/remote/secondary authority intersection that profiles cannot bypass.
Bind existing Action, ResourceAuthority, CanonicalResource, and action/resource compatibility primitives reused by the compiler.
Bind ValidatedGrant round-trip validation, exact subject/runtime binding, finite envelope, and hierarchy rules.
Bind authoritative consequence ordering/classification and typed conjunctive constraint narrowing.
Bind the complete original SG-000025 scope, safety, acceptance, evidence, and change surface.
Bind the supported Grain -> explicit context -> WorkPacket -> execute -> independent proof lifecycle and packet authority boundary.

outcome: Implement Safe, Standard, Developer, Autonomous, and Custom as deterministic, provider-neutral policy inputs that compile one trusted bounded intent into one or more exact-action finite Grant candidates without creating an alternate authorization path, bypassing consequence classification, or performing side effects.

risk.recovery: Revert only SG-000025 profile refinement/implementation/closeout changes and keep KX-P02-S05-T02 at NEXT. Preserve S05-T01 policy/store/daemon semantics, all existing Grant/audit rows, tracked original WorkPacket evidence, and canonical ledgers; never weaken existing admission or advance S06 on failed profile proof.

scope_in: Add a repository-owned pure profile compiler to kernux-policy; profiles are convenience inputs, never an authorization or side-effect execution path.

Add adversarial tests proving profile names cannot self-authorize, untrusted provenance cannot widen profiles, preset ordering is not treated as blanket inheritance, malformed/unknown/custom ambiguity denies, and every emitted Grant remains finite/exact and accepted by existing validation.

After native SpecGrain verification and protected closeout, advance only KX-P02-S05-T02 to PROVEN and KX-P02-S06-T01 to NEXT if live canonical truth still permits it; keep S06-T02 PLANNED and P02 exit unproven.

Autonomous may compile broader explicitly requested task/runtime/sandbox intents only when authoritative consequence is at most C2 and the action is not an authority-management or secret-reveal action; exact resources, finite budgets, runtime isolation/policy and all mandatory authority layers remain active.

Compile only trusted profile intents already bound to an exact Run, optional exact AgentSession, exact Runtime revision, one exact action, canonical resource, explicit exact/subtree scope, validated constraints, finite trusted time window, positive finite max-use budget, issuer authority, and policy revision.

Custom uses explicit trusted granular rules with exact action, allowed resource authority/scope, maximum consequence, and constraint ceilings; absence, ambiguity, wildcard, unknown action/resource, or incomparable constraints fails closed.

Developer may additionally compile bounded sandbox process/PTY and project git.modify intents while keeping publish/admin, secret access, host-system authority, policy/grant/identity mutation, and C3/C4 effects outside preset auto-grant semantics.

Persist the original SpecGrain ContextSource set and WorkPacket bytes before the first profile implementation slice, and require byte-identical replay from the tracked sources before implementation proceeds.

Profile compilation never permits policy.modify, grant.issue, grant.delegate, identity.manage, or secret.reveal through preset automation; these authority/credential-expanding surfaces require their existing explicit policy path.

Qualify bounded implementation on Linux CI, native Windows protected CI, and native macOS; require full pnpm check, Diffcipline R3, Alibaba OpenCodeReview Delegation Mode accounting, exact-head semantic review with zero unresolved threads, ordinary merge, and exact post-merge six-job qualification before native proof/closeout.
Represent exactly Safe, Standard, Developer, Autonomous, and Custom with deterministic closed semantics and no provider-native permission strings or wildcard actions/resources.

Return bounded Grant candidates that must still pass existing ValidatedGrant validation, durable issuance/audit, consequence classification, mandatory authority intersection, runtime-capability checks, remote-host checks, secondary-resource checks, and pre-side-effect admission.

Safe automatically admits only low-risk project/workspace observation intents that remain C0 and excludes writes, process/PTY execution, network/browser mutation, clipboard, secrets, policy/grant/identity mutation, and external side effects.

Standard may compile project-scoped read/write and bounded local artifact intents up to C1; automatic process execution is permitted only for an explicitly isolated sandbox resource and remains constrained/finite. Secrets, authority changes, publish/commit, and other C2+ external effects remain gated.
scope_out: Do not add new KRP fields, core actions, resource authorities, consequence classes, external policy engines, expression languages, or provider-specific permission models.
Do not advance S06 or P02 phase exit from implementation evidence alone; native proof, protected closeout, and canonical transition remain separate governed steps.
Do not create immortal Grants, wildcard actions/resources/runtimes, unlimited use budgets, unbounded lifetimes, delegation-by-default, or a hidden allow-all Autonomous mode.
Do not implement approval UI, desktop renderer policy UX, profile editor UI, or organization/team policy distribution.
Do not implement filesystem/process/PTY/Git/browser/computer/network side-effect executors; profiles only compile bounded authorization candidates.
Do not implement secret-provider adapters, secret plaintext access/reveal, credential injection, or OS credential-store integration; KX-P02-S06-T01 owns secret brokerage.

Do not let profile choice, UI text, model/tool/browser/document/provider content, or a profile name substitute for C4 authorization, trusted policy state, runtime capability, or existing Grant admission.
